attempt_order: ascending candidate_id (a SHA-256 digest, so uncorrelated with difficulty)
limitations: Ten rows from ONE family. The families are not interchangeable; this scores `integer-absolute-value`, not the held-out population.
Scored by an agent with the whole repository available, which is the condition the system operates under -- not a measurement of a cold, retrieval-free prover.

The result is a lower bound on difficulty for this family only: every row turned out to be reachable from `Int.le` and `Int.mul` being four-case COMPUTING definitions in this construction, which Mathlib's own proofs do not use and which does not transfer to families whose content is not constructor-shaped.

partition_integrity.note: No drawn row changed partition or membership. The digest is over the sorted (fact_id, partition) pairs of BOTH manifests, pinned at the protocol commit and unchanged after scoring. Its negative control -- recomputing with one row's partition flipped and requiring the digest to move -- runs on every invocation.

selection_rule: The lexicographically first held-out family name in nursery-v2-extension.json, skipping any family from which the scoring lane had already been exposed to a statement before the protocol was committed. `descent-and-well-ordering` was excluded on that clause and the exposure is disclosed in the protocol; the rule then selects `integer-absolute-value`.

spends.note: Scoring a family SPENDS it: a proof route for one member is evidence about its siblings, which is why the split key is <family>:<statement-shape>. This record exists so that spend is on the books rather than inferred from a diff. `descent-and-well-ordering` carries a one-row statement exposure (F:ml430-int-exists-greatest-of-bdd-540c90cf), disclosed in the protocol and NOT scored here.
